evals.name: topic-action-runs-mission-interview
evals.expected_output: Routes to the topic action (start-or-resume). For a new rust-ownership workspace it creates the workspace and runs the mission interview (WHY, goal, success criteria) before teaching; if one already exists it resumes from saved state. Either way it opens with orientation, not a lecture dump.
expectations: Routes to the `topic` action and resolves the workspace root per the workspace-root resolution ladder — in a headless session with nothing configured this falls through to the plugin's persistent data directory, and never lands in the consuming repo's working tree
For a new workspace, runs the mission interview (WHY / goal / success) before teaching; for an existing one, resumes from saved state rather than re-interviewing from scratch
Does not open by lecturing content before the mission is established or prior state is loaded

evals.name: smart-default-detects-codebase-vs-topic
evals.prompt: /education:teach the auth-flow module in this repo
evals.expected_output: With no explicit action and a subject naming a repo-grounded concept, resolves to codebase mode and grounds in files discovered at teach-time; if discovery finds no real grounding for the concept in this repo, it asks the user to point to the relevant area rather than inventing repo sources.
expectations: Detects that the subject names a repo-grounded concept and resolves to `codebase` mode (not `topic`)
Discovers grounding from live repo files at teach-time (climbs for CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, surveys structure) rather than baked assumptions
If no real grounding for the concept is found in the repo, asks the user to point to the relevant area instead of inventing or hallucinating repo sources

evals.name: primer-creates-no-workspace
evals.prompt: /education:teach primer color-grading — I just need enough vocabulary to direct the work now.
evals.expected_output: Runs the single-session primer with NO workspace, glossary, or learning records. It first intakes the user's starting point with one question, then builds the vocabulary ladder (terms, quality axes, good-vs-bad examples, a prompt template).
expectations: Creates NO workspace directory, glossary, or learning records for the primer (single-session, no persistence)

Opens by intaking the user's starting point with one question, then builds the vocabulary ladder — core terms, the quality axes experts judge by, worked good-vs-bad examples, and a closing prompt template
Offers to escalate to `/education:teach topic color-grading` for depth rather than silently starting a full workspace

evals.name: coach-one-question-at-a-time
evals.prompt: /education:teach topic binary-search-trees — I want to understand how deletion works.
evals.expected_output: Adopts coach posture from the first turn: opens with a single question (the mission interview for a new workspace, or a teaching-dialog question in an active one), asks one question at a time, and never opens by lecturing the whole deletion algorithm.
expectations: Opens with ONE question and waits, rather than front-loading a full explanation
Leads with questions before explanations, per coach-not-lecturer posture (the mission interview itself is one-question-at-a-time)
Does not dump the complete deletion algorithm in a single lecture turn

evals.name: ground-in-primary-sources-not-recall
evals.expected_output: For a new workspace it runs the mission interview before teaching; and whenever it teaches the Knowledge layer for this fast-moving framework, it grounds claims in primary sources fetched or files Read this turn (RESOURCES.md / official docs), never parametric recall, since library/framework facts drift.
expectations: Respects the new-workspace flow — runs the mission interview / resource seeding before delivering Knowledge content, rather than jumping straight into framework facts
Any Knowledge-layer claim that drives a lesson is grounded in a source fetched or a file Read this turn, not training-data recall
Does not assert volatile framework facts from memory — pulls from RESOURCES.md / documentation sources for this fast-moving topic

evals.name: no-silent-workspace-invention
evals.expected_output: The explain action requires an active workspace to write concepts/<concept>/ into, and never silently invents one. It resolves against the live workspace state: uses the single existing workspace when exactly one exists, asks which when several exist, and asks whether to start one (topic/codebase) when none exists — so the correct behavior depends on the current workspace state rather than being a fixed branch.
expectations: Recognizes that `explain` requires an active workspace to write concepts/<concept>/ into
Never silently invents or fabricates a workspace — it resolves against the live existing workspace state before writing
Takes the branch that matches the current state: use the one existing workspace, ask which when several exist, or ask whether to start one when none exists

evals.name: research-grounding-tier-selection
evals.prompt: /education:teach codebase hooks-system — teach me how this repo's hook scripts work.
evals.expected_output: Codebase-mode lesson claims ground in repo files Read this turn (tier 0 of the research-grounding ladder) with no research dispatch spawned for them; a tier-1 research dispatch is reserved for contested, broad, or fast-domain external claims and stays within roughly one dispatch per session. No lesson-driving claim comes from parametric recall at any tier.
expectations: Grounds codebase-mode lesson claims in repo files Read this turn (tier 0), without dispatching a research subagent for them
Escalates to a tier-1 research dispatch only for contested, broad, or fast-domain external claims — batching open questions to stay within roughly one dispatch per session
Never asserts a lesson-driving claim from parametric recall at any tier — the ladder decides which fetch, never whether

evals.name: workspace-root-ladder-resolution
evals.expected_output: Before creating the workspace it resolves the root ladder in order — project declaration, workspace_root userConfig, one-time ask (interactive only), the OS Documents 'Claude Learning' home when Documents exists and differs from $HOME (topic mode only), then plugin data. A surviving ${user_config.workspace_root} literal is treated as unset and never pasted into a shell command, and the platform Documents directory is never created by the skill.
expectations: Resolves the workspace root by the documented ladder order (project declaration → workspace_root userConfig → ask-once → OS Documents home → plugin-data fallback) rather than hardcoding one location
Treats a surviving ${user_config.workspace_root} literal as unset and never pastes it into a shell command
Applies the mode split: the Documents default is topic-mode only; codebase workspaces stay under plugin data absent explicit project-declaration or userConfig rooting
Never creates the platform Documents directory itself, and keeps existing plugin-data workspaces readable (the fallback root is always scanned)

evals.name: lesson-format-platform-aware
evals.prompt: /education:teach explain css-grid — I'm at my desktop with a browser available.
evals.expected_output: With a render-capable host the lesson defaults to interactive, self-contained lesson.html — shared assets spliced in from the workspace assets/ library rather than re-authored, quiz block with shuffled answers ending in a copy-out result block the learner pastes back for grading — while a headless/SSH/cloud host would get lesson.md. The durable trio (reference.md, learning records, GLOSSARY.md) stays markdown either way, and after writing it offers (permission-gated, never auto-runs) the platform-appropriate open command.
expectations: Defaults to interactive self-contained lesson.html when the host can render it and to lesson.md on headless/remote hosts — one lesson file per concept either way
Splices the shared stylesheet and quiz component from the workspace assets/ library instead of re-emitting them inline per lesson
Keeps the durable trio (reference.md, learning records, GLOSSARY.md) markdown regardless of lesson format
Offers to open the written lesson via the platform-appropriate command, permission-gated, and skips the offer on remote/web/cloud hosts

evals.name: resume-surfaces-due-for-review
evals.expected_output: Resume reads MISSION/GLOSSARY/NOTES, scans learning records for the frontier, and surfaces due-for-review floor concepts (record age weighed against domain velocity) BEFORE advancing — opening with a quick retrieval question on a due concept when any exist, rather than re-lecturing it.
expectations: Surfaces due-for-review concepts computed from learning-record age × domain velocity before advancing the frontier
Opens with a retrieval question on a due floor concept when one exists, rather than re-lecturing the content
Loads per-concept due-for-review detail only on resume of that workspace — status stays one line per workspace from filename/mtime heuristics

evals.name: deictic-subject-routes-codebase-stable-name
evals.expected_output: A deictic whole-repo subject routes to codebase mode via the smart default, and the workspace gets a stable content name derived from the repo basename plus a scope word (raw name like '<repo-basename> overview'), recorded as the raw subject name — never a slug of the deictic phrase itself.
expectations: Routes the whole-repo/deictic subject ('this repo') to codebase mode via the smart default
Derives a stable content name (repo basename + scope word) recorded as the raw subject name, instead of slugging the deixis into something like 'this-repo'
Resolves two runs of the same deictic request to the same workspace
